items.q: A 23-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset, severe, colicky right lower quadrant pain associated with nausea and two episodes of vomiting. Transvaginal pelvic ultrasound reveals an enlarged right ovary measuring 7.5 cm with peripheral displaced follicles and absent arterial and venous Doppler flow. What is the definitive management of choice?
o: Immediate diagnostic laparoscopy with surgical detorsion of the right ovary
Immediate right salpingo-oophorectomy to prevent pulmonary embolism
Intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics and close observation for 24 hours
items.exp: The clinical presentation and Doppler ultrasound findings are diagnostic of acute adnexal (ovarian) torsion. The management of choice in a reproductive-age woman is immediate diagnostic laparoscopy with conservative surgical detorsion. Multiple studies confirm that detorsion preserves viable ovarian follicular reserve in > 90% of cases and does not cause pulmonary embolism.
r: Correct. Emergency laparoscopy with detorsion is the standard fertility-preserving management.
Incorrect. Oophorectomy is aggressive overtreatment; ischemic-appearing ovaries recover function after detorsion.
Incorrect. Antibiotics and observation will result in complete irreversible ovarian necrosis.
Incorrect. Needle aspiration does not correct the vascular twist and risks spillage.
items.kp: Acute adnexal torsion is an emergency treated by immediate laparoscopy and conservative detorsion to salvage ovarian function.

items.q: Which tissue element is responsible for the characteristic Rokitansky protuberance seen on ultrasound and gross pathology in a mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst)?
o: Solid prominence of ectodermal tissue containing hair, sebaceous glands and teeth
items.exp: The Rokitansky protuberance (dermoid plug) is a solid, raised mural prominence projecting into the cyst cavity of a mature cystic teratoma. It is composed predominantly of ectodermal tissues, including sebaceous glands, hair follicles, bone, and teeth, and produces high-level acoustic shadowing on ultrasound.
r: Correct. The Rokitansky nodule is the ectodermal mural plug containing hair, sebum, and dental structures.
Incorrect. Malignant transformation occurs in only 1-2% of teratomas, usually into squamous cell carcinoma.
Incorrect. Theca interna hyperplasia is seen in theca lutein cysts, not dermoid teratomas.
Incorrect. Mucinous crypts define mucinous cystadenomas.
items.kp: The Rokitansky protuberance is the solid ectodermal mural plug in a mature cystic teratoma containing hair, teeth, and bone.

items.q: A 26-year-old woman is found to have an asymptomatic 4.5 cm unilocular, thin-walled, anechoic right ovarian cyst on routine transvaginal ultrasound. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Reassurance and repeat pelvic ultrasound in 6 to 8 weeks
Measurement of serum CA-125, CEA and AFP
Oral combined contraceptives to shrink the existing cyst
items.exp: An asymptomatic unilocular, thin-walled, anechoic cyst < 5-8 cm in a premenopausal woman is virtually always a physiological functional cyst (follicular cyst). The recommended management is reassurance and expectant observation with repeat ultrasound in 6 to 8 weeks (after 1-2 menstrual cycles), as > 70% resolve spontaneously. Oral contraceptives do not shrink pre-existing cysts.
r: Correct. Expectant management with repeat ultrasound in 6-8 weeks confirms spontaneous resolution of functional cysts.
Incorrect. Surgery is overtreatment for small, benign-appearing physiological cysts.
Incorrect. Tumor markers are non-specific and unnecessary in simple physiological cysts.
Incorrect. Oral contraceptives prevent new cyst formation but do not hasten resolution of existing cysts.
items.kp: Simple anechoic ovarian cysts < 5 cm in premenopausal women are physiological and should be managed expectantly for 6-8 weeks.

items.q: What is the typical ultrasound appearance of an ovarian endometrioma ('chocolate cyst')?
o: Homogeneous, low-level internal echoes ('ground-glass' appearance) without internal vascularity
Anechoic simple cyst with posterior acoustic enhancement
Complex mass with bright mural calcifications and acoustic shadow
Multiloculated cystic mass with thick papillary excrescences and high Doppler flow
items.exp: Ovarian endometriomas characteristically appear on transvaginal ultrasound as homogeneous, unilocular or multilocular cystic masses containing uniform, low-level internal echoes (classic 'ground-glass' echogenicity) resulting from layered, hemolyzed menstrual blood, without internal mural vascularity.
r: Correct. Homogeneous low-level 'ground-glass' echogenicity is the hallmark sonographic feature of endometrioma.
Incorrect. Anechoic simple cysts represent follicular or serous cysts.
Incorrect. Mural calcifications with acoustic shadowing represent dermoid cysts.
Incorrect. Thick papillary projections with high Doppler flow raise suspicion for malignancy.
items.kp: An endometrioma characteristically presents on ultrasound as a cystic mass with homogeneous low-level 'ground-glass' echoes.

items.q: Which complication is specifically associated with the intraoperative rupture or leakage of a large mucinous cystadenoma of the ovary?
items.exp: Rupture of an ovarian mucinous neoplasm (especially borderline or low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms with ovarian involvement) can seed the peritoneal cavity with mucin-secreting epithelial cells, producing progressive, gelatinous ascites known as pseudomyxoma peritonei ('jelly belly').
r: Correct. Mucin spillage into the peritoneal cavity can lead to pseudomyxoma peritonei.
Incorrect. Chemical peritonitis occurs from rupture of a dermoid cyst spilling sebaceous fluid.
Incorrect. Hemolytic anemia is not triggered by mucinous fluid.
Incorrect. Fat embolism does not occur from mucinous cysts.
items.kp: Rupture of a mucinous neoplasm can seed the peritoneal cavity, predisposing to pseudomyxoma peritonei.

items.q: What is the primary vascular mechanism leading to hemorrhagic infarction and gangrene in acute adnexal torsion?
o: Initial occlusion of low-pressure venous and lymphatic drainage leading to congestion, followed by arterial cessation
Primary abrupt spasm of the abdominal aorta
Septic embolization from the pelvic veins
Rupture of the internal iliac artery
items.exp: When the ovarian pedicle twists, the thin-walled, low-pressure venous and lymphatic vessels are compressed first, while high-pressure arterial inflow continues. This results in massive ovarian edema, passive congestion, and extravasation of blood into the stroma, creating high tissue pressure that eventually halts arterial inflow, causing ischemia and hemorrhagic necrosis.
r: Correct. Venous and lymphatic occlusion occurs first, causing congestion and edema that subsequently terminates arterial inflow.
Incorrect. Torsion does not affect the abdominal aorta.
Incorrect. Torsion is a mechanical twisting event, not septic embolization.
Incorrect. The internal iliac artery does not rupture.
items.kp: Adnexal torsion occludes venous outflow first, causing massive stromal congestion before arterial perfusion ceases.

items.q: In a 20-year-old woman undergoing laparoscopy for acute adnexal torsion, the right ovary appears dark purple and congested after untwisting. What is the correct surgical management?
o: Untwist the adnexa, observe for reperfusion, and preserve the ovary
Inject high-dose heparin directly into the ovarian cortex
items.exp: Modern evidence strongly dictates that visual appearance at the time of detorsion does not correlate with histological necrosis or subsequent functional viability. Over 90% of bluish-black, congested ovaries recover normal endocrine and ovulatory function. The correct practice is conservative detorsion and ovarian preservation.
r: Correct. Untwisting and preserving the ovary allows remarkable functional recovery even in dark, congested ovaries.
Incorrect. Oophorectomy unnecessarily castrates young women based on misleading visual congestion.
Incorrect. Bilateral oophorectomy is completely contraindicated.
Incorrect. Direct cortical heparin injection carries severe hemorrhage risk with no proven benefit.
items.kp: Congested, dark ischemic ovaries should be conservatively untwisted and preserved, as over 90% regain normal function.

items.q: Which benign ovarian mass is composed predominantly of mature thyroid tissue and can occasionally present with symptoms of clinical hyperthyroidism?
items.exp: Struma ovarii is a specialized, monodermal mature teratoma composed predominantly (> 50%) or entirely of mature thyroid tissue. In approximately 5-10% of cases, the functional thyroid tissue secretes excessive thyroxine, causing clinical hyperthyroidism (thyrotoxicosis) with an empty cervical thyroid gland on scintigraphy.
r: Correct. Struma ovarii is a monodermal teratoma composed of thyroid tissue that can cause hyperthyroidism.
Incorrect. Granulosa cell tumor secretes estrogen, causing endometrial hyperplasia and precocious puberty.
Incorrect. Dysgerminoma is a malignant germ cell tumor secreting LDH.
Incorrect. Ovarian fibroma is a benign stromal tumor associated with Meigs syndrome.
items.kp: Struma ovarii is a monodermal teratoma composed of mature thyroid tissue capable of inducing clinical hyperthyroidism.

items.q: What triad of clinical features defines Meigs syndrome?
o: Benign ovarian fibroma, ascites, and right-sided pleural effusion
Granulosa cell tumor, precocious puberty, and uterine bleeding
items.exp: Meigs syndrome is characterized by the classic triad of a benign solid ovarian fibroma (or fibrothecoma), ascites, and pleural effusion (typically right-sided). Both the ascites and pleural fluid resolve completely and permanently following surgical excision of the ovarian fibroma.
r: Correct. Meigs syndrome consists of benign ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion, resolving after tumor removal.
Incorrect. Dermoid with hirsutism is not Meigs syndrome.
Incorrect. Granulosa cell tumor with precocious puberty reflects estrogenic hypersecretion.
Incorrect. Endometrioma triad reflects pelvic endometriosis.
items.kp: Meigs syndrome consists of a benign ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion, completely resolving after cystectomy.

items.q: A pregnant woman at 10 weeks gestation with complete hydatidiform mole has bilateral, symmetrically enlarged ovaries measuring 10 cm each, composed of multiple thin-walled cysts resembling a 'soap-bubble' appearance. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: Theca lutein cysts develop secondary to massive ovarian stimulation by markedly elevated circulating levels of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), classically in molar pregnancy or multiple gestations. They present as bilateral, multiloculated large ovaries and spontaneously regress following evacuation of the mole.
r: Correct. Theca lutein cysts are bilateral multilocular cysts caused by excessive hCG stimulation in molar pregnancy.
Incorrect. Bilateral epithelial ovarian carcinoma is rare in young pregnant women and lacks the characteristic history.
Incorrect. PCOS ovaries are smaller (< 10-15 mL volume) with subcapsular peripheral follicles.
Incorrect. Bilateral dermoids contain solid components, fat, and calcifications, not soap-bubble multilocular cysts.
items.kp: Theca lutein cysts are bilateral, multilocular cysts caused by massive hCG stimulation that regress after molar evacuation.
